extra.message: The unauthenticated GET /api/v2/user route passes the user-controlled query parameter directly to eval(): res.send('Welcome name ' + eval(req.query.name)). An attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server via a request like /api/v2/user?name=require('child_process').execSync('id').toString(), resulting in full remote code execution.

The /contact route extracts the url query parameter from the request (url.parse(req.url, true).query) and passes it directly to needle.get() with no validation or allowlist. An unauthenticated attacker can force the server to make requests to arbitrary internal targets (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000, cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254), enabling Server-Side Request Forgery.

res.redirect(query.url) redirects the caller to a fully attacker-controlled URL taken from the ?url= query parameter with no validation. This is an open redirect that can be used for phishing (e.g. /contact?url=https://evil.com) while appearing to originate from the trusted application domain.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: POST /api/v2/profile passes the user-controlled object req.body.profile directly as the view locals: res.render('profile', profile). The header partial rendered by this view (public/templates/partials/header.hbs:39) outputs the 'body' local with a triple-stash {{{body}}}, which performs no HTML escaping. A request body like {"profile":{"body":""}} is rendered as raw HTML/JavaScript, enabling cross-site scripting that executes in the logged-in user's browser.

GET /api/v1/users/:name is registered without the auth middleware (unlike the /api/v2 profile endpoints) and returns the matched user document (res.send(user) at line 250 exposes _id, name, email, age). Any unauthenticated caller can enumerate and retrieve any user's personal information by name.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/users/:id fetches the target with User.findById(req.params.id) and applies the submitted updates to whatever user that id belongs to, with no ownership check against the authenticated req.user. Any authenticated user can change any other user's name, email, and password, resulting in complete account takeover.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DELETE /api/v1/users/:id calls User.findByIdAndDelete(req.params.id) without verifying that the id belongs to the authenticated user. Any logged-in user can permanently delete any other account (and cascade-delete that user's tasks).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: On user registration, the session JWT is set with res.cookie('auth_token', token) without httpOnly, Secure, or SameSite options. The authentication token is readable by JavaScript (so any XSS in the application allows session token theft) and is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: On login (POST /dashboard), the session JWT is set with res.cookie('auth_token', token) without httpOnly, Secure, or SameSite options. The authentication token is readable by JavaScript (so any XSS in the application allows session token theft) and is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: GET /api/v1/tasks is registered without the auth middleware and executes Task.find({}), returning every task belonging to every user to any unauthenticated caller. All users' task data is disclosed without authentication.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/tasks/:id fetches the task with Task.findById(req.params.id) with no owner filter (unlike the v2 equivalent at line 56 which adds owner: req.user._id). Any authenticated user can modify any other user's task, including overwriting a victim's task description with attacker-controlled content.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Session tokens are signed with the hardcoded secret 'hardsecret': jwt.sign({ _id: user._id.toString() }, 'hardsecret'). Anyone with access to this source can forge valid authentication tokens for any user id, completely bypassing authentication.

jwt.sign() is called without an expiresIn option and no expiry claim is set, so authentication tokens never expire. A stolen or leaked token remains valid indefinitely unless the user manually logs out of all sessions (tokens are only cleared in the logout/logoutAll handlers).

The authentication middleware verifies tokens with the same hardcoded secret 'hardsecret' (jwt.verify(token, 'hardsecret')). Combined with the hardcoded signing secret in src/models/user.js:71, an attacker can forge arbitrary valid tokens and authenticate as any user.

Task descriptions returned by the API are rendered without escaping via newListItem.innerHTML = `...${todo.description}...`. HTML is only stripped client-side on input (stripHTML in handleSubmitForm/editTodo), so descriptions written directly to the REST API (or planted in a victim's task via the IDOR on PATCH /api/v1/tasks/:id) execute as stored DOM-based XSS when the victim's dashboard loads.

Profile data fetched from /api/v2/profile (data.user.name and other fields, which are stored without any server-side HTML sanitization) is interpolated into a template literal and assigned to document.getElementById(dataId).innerHTML. A name containing HTML/JavaScript (set at registration, via PATCH, or injected into a victim's account via the IDOR on PATCH /api/v1/users/:id) executes in the victim's browser as stored DOM-based XSS.

The inline script reads the name parameter from window.location.search (getQueryParameter) and concatenates it unescaped into an HTML string that is assigned to resultsEl.innerHTML (line 190). A crafted link such as /contact.html?name= executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser (reflected DOM-based XSS).
